sanctuary_sites: CNS (uncommon in adult AML; relatively increased in monocytic subtypes and hyperleukocytosis)
heme_involvement_pattern.staging_system: Not staged in TNM sense; risk-stratified by cytogenetics/molecular (ELN 2022) into favourable/intermediate/adverse.

biomarkers.name: Cytogenetics (karyotype)
biomarkers.clinical_use: ELN 2022 risk: favourable (t(8;21), inv(16)/t(16;16), mutated NPM1 without adverse-risk cytogenetics, bZIP in-frame mutated CEBPA); intermediate; adverse (complex karyotype, monosomal karyotype, -5/del(5q), -7, del(17p)/abn(17p), inv(3)/t(3;3), t(6;9), certain KMT2A rearrangements, MECOM rearrangement). Drives transplant decisions

biomarkers.name: FLT3-ITD
biomarkers.clinical_use: Associated with increased relapse risk; ELN 2022 no longer uses FLT3-ITD allelic ratio in risk assignment. Predictive: midostaurin (RATIFY) added to intensive induction; gilteritinib for R/R; quizartinib + chemotherapy first-line in selected regulatory settings

biomarkers.name: FLT3-TKD (D835)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Predictive for FLT3 inhibitor-based therapy, including gilteritinib; midostaurin also has activity

biomarkers.name: NPM1
biomarkers.clinical_use: Favourable in ELN 2022 when mutated in the absence of adverse-risk cytogenetics. Excellent MRD marker by RT-qPCR — MRD kinetics guide post-remission strategy

biomarkers.name: IDH1 R132 / IDH2 R140, R172
biomarkers.clinical_use: Ivosidenib (IDH1) and enasidenib (IDH2) — approved single-agent and in combinations (ivosidenib + azacitidine first-line unfit)

biomarkers.name: TP53
biomarkers.prevalence: ~5-10% de novo; enriched in therapy-related AML and AML with myelodysplasia-related changes
biomarkers.clinical_use: Very adverse; recognised as a distinct entity in ICC 2022. Historically poor outcomes with venetoclax + azacitidine and with intensive chemotherapy

biomarkers.name: CEBPA biallelic (or basic leucine zipper — bZIP)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Favourable — current classifications emphasise in-frame bZIP CEBPA-mutated AML as a distinct favourable-risk entity

biomarkers.name: ASXL1, RUNX1, EZH2, SF3B1, SRSF2, U2AF1, ZRSR2, BCOR, STAG2, SETBP1 (MDS-related mutations)
biomarkers.clinical_use: These mutations define AML myelodysplasia-related in WHO 2022/ICC 2022 when present in the appropriate setting (excluding AML with defining recurrent genetic abnormalities) and generally confer adverse risk

biomarkers.name: KIT mutations
biomarkers.prevalence: Subset of core-binding factor AML, especially t(8;21)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Associated with higher relapse risk in some CBF AML series, particularly t(8;21); prognostic effect is less consistent than historically reported

biomarkers.name: CD33
biomarkers.clinical_use: Gemtuzumab ozogamicin (anti-CD33 ADC) — benefit shown when added to induction in selected newly diagnosed AML, particularly favourable/intermediate-risk disease

biomarkers.name: Measurable residual disease (MRD) — flow or molecular
biomarkers.clinical_use: Post-induction and post-consolidation MRD status guides transplant referral; NPM1 and CBF-AML MRD kinetics are highly predictive of relapse

biomarkers.name: Venetoclax + azacitidine responsiveness / BAX-BAK
biomarkers.clinical_use: VIALE-A regimen: standard for older/unfit AML. Responses are generally lower in TP53-mutated AML; resistance biology is evolving, but BAX/BAK is not an established routine clinical biomarker

biomarkers.name: Core-binding factor fusions: RUNX1::RUNX1T1 and CBFB::MYH11
biomarkers.clinical_use: Define favourable-risk AML in ELN 2022; diagnosis requires cytogenetic/molecular confirmation and transcript levels can be followed for MRD

biomarkers.name: PML::RARA
biomarkers.clinical_use: Defines acute promyelocytic leukaemia (APL), a separate entity rather than AML, NOS; predicts sensitivity to ATRA and arsenic trioxide

biomarkers.name: KMT2A rearrangements
biomarkers.clinical_use: Recurrent genetic abnormality in AML; prognosis varies by partner, with several subtypes classified as adverse risk in ELN 2022

histomorphological_subtype.primary_pattern: Blast proliferation (usually ≥20% myeloblasts in blood or marrow) with myeloid differentiation; Auer rods diagnostic when present
variants: FAB M0-M7 legacy classification (M3 = APL, separate entity)
WHO 2022 lineage-based subtypes: myeloid, monocytic, erythroid, megakaryoblastic differentiation

AML defined by differentiation (WHO 2022): AML with minimal differentiation, without maturation, with maturation, acute monoblastic/monocytic leukaemia, pure erythroid leukaemia, acute megakaryoblastic leukaemia
histomorphological_subtype.grading: Not graded; genetic risk stratification (ELN 2022: favourable, intermediate, adverse) drives management

tumor_microenvironment.immune_context: Bone marrow niche dependency — leukaemia stem cells interact with mesenchymal stromal cells; some subsets are immunologically distinct, but immune checkpoint inhibitor monotherapy has been disappointing overall
tumor_microenvironment.stromal_features: Bone marrow infiltration displacing normal haematopoiesis; blast morphology defines lineage

cellular_states_and_lineage.cell_of_origin: Haematopoietic stem cell (HSC) or committed myeloid progenitor with maturation arrest
cellular_states_and_lineage.developmental_lineage: Mesoderm — haematopoietic system (arising from haemogenic endothelium during embryogenesis; adult HSCs reside in bone marrow niche)
cellular_states_and_lineage.differentiation_state: Myeloid maturation arrest at variable stages — myeloid, monocytic, erythroid, or megakaryocytic differentiation programmes may be preserved; leukaemia stem cells (LSCs) sustain disease, often enriched in CD34+/CD38- fractions but immunophenotypically heterogeneous
cellular_states_and_lineage.lineage_plasticity: LSC hierarchy with variable maturation arrest driven by different genetic events; treatment can select for LSC-enriched populations at relapse; lineage switching is rare
